newsitem.title: UK: Cook sees no snub in China leaders missing banquet.
newsitem.headline: Cook sees no snub in China leaders missing banquet.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng will not attend a farewell banquet in Hong Kong on Monday shortly before Britain hands the colony back to China, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Sunday.
But Cook denied that their absence would be a snub, telling BBC Television's Breakfast with Frost programme in Hong Kong that Britain had never expected them to attend.

"The fact of the matter is we never expected them to be at the farewell (banquet) ceremony.... That's what I understood to be the case when I left London, that's what we've understood to be the case for the last two months," Cook said.
"In the plans for those two gentlemen, nothing has changed," he added.

Jiang, who is also head of the Communist Party and commander-in-chief of the armed forces, is expected to cross the border into Hong Kong shortly before the handover ceremonies at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.

After crossing the border and within hours of the entry of 509 People's Liberation Army troops, Jiang and Li are due to sail across Victoria Harbour to Hong Kong island to receive the territory back from Prince Charles, Britain's heir to the throne.
"We do expect Jiang Zemin and Li Peng to be both at the handover ceremony. We understand that they are both going to be there," Cook said.
He said China would be represented at the banquet by Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.

"That's quite normal. I'm afraid I've become accustomed as foreign secretary to the fact that is is the function of foreign secretaries to eat for the nation, and that's what Qian Qichen will be doing," Cook quipped.
